physical.title: textile; cloth
physical.summary: Cloth (Yoruba aso oke), composed of 16 hand-woven narrow strips, hand-woven from imported cotton, and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The ground weave is entirely white in the warp and most of the weft, though the weft also has lines of pink; there is a supplementary weft in purple but in no other colour. Each of the two outer strips has an individual design, one with pairs of pink lines in the weft, the other with six pattern blocks arranged regularly along its length with hour-glass designs in purple bordered by bands of pink. The 14 strips in the centre of the cloth all have the same design, which is more or less accurately aligned across the cloth. There are three bands of decoration using (a) diamond shapes formed by discontinuous ground weft in pink, (b) hour-glass shapes formed by supplementary weft in purple, and (c) stripes with open-work created by binding the weft. The ends have been hemmed by hand.
